steps.text: Tear the kale leaves into bite-size pieces from the thick stems; discard the stems.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook and stir the garlic in the hot oil until softened, about 2 minutes. Add the kale and continue cooking and stirring until the kale is bright green and wilted, about 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Kale
raw_recipe.description: A delicious, garlicky way to cook the underused, antioxidant rich kale!
raw_recipe.name: Garlic Kale

review.reviewBody: I love Kale and I use this method often. I eat a lot of Kale, and unless its fresh from the garden (usually after the first frost), I tend to cook it for around 15 minutes to prevent it tasting rubbery. First if I have a large bunch of kale I'll thinly slice a whole bulb of garlic, because I love garlic. If I add the garlic first, it burns, so I cook the kale for a good 10 minutes before adding the garlic. To cut down on oil, I'll cut up the kale and then rinse it off in the strainer. I use the water left on the kale leaves combined with a dash of oil to saute it. And finally I add some salt and pepper.

This is the first time I have ate or cooked kale, we are believers! I used baby kale and baby spinach bc I didn't have enough baby kale. I did not have to steam or massage salt into leaves bc the baby Kale is tender and not the slightest bitter. I used a hot heavy cast iron skillet and added bacon drippings and added 4 cloves smashed garlic to pan over medium heat. Cook until slightly tan and remove from pan, this infuses drippings with garlicky goodness, then I added 8 oz of sliced mushrooms and caramelized. Then I added 5 oz Kale and 8 oz spinach, bc that is what I had on hand, I sautéed greens until wilted and sprinkled liberally with coarse kosher salt. Last 5 minutes I grated 4 large garlic cloves, this allows the garlic time to cook some of the raw flavor out, mellowing slightly, yet not so much you miss that garlic flavor you crave. Once I added the greens to serving bowl I squeezed a lemon wedge over to give the greens a little brightness. We devoured, devoured them! My husband was rooting thru the fridge for left-overs, and asked that I make this side dish regularly. We are now Kale converts! :)

Good! I used about 1/2 cup chopped onions, and sauteed them for about 5 min before adding the kale (2/3 bag of pre-chopped kale). With the kale, I added about 1/2 cup water and let the kale steam with the lid on the pan. After it softened, I drained it and added the garlic, a little sea salt, fresh ground pepper, and squeezed about 1/2 a fresh lemon over the top and cooked for about a minute or two. I removed it from the heat and added about a cup of canellini beans and some freshly shredded asiago cheese.

**odd note!***

Along with this dish I made a Caprese salad, which included a balsamic reduction made from 1 cup balsamic vinegar brought to a boil with 1/3 cup honey, and then reduced the heat and simmered about 10 min until the sauce was reduced to about 1/3 cup. This sauce accidentally seeped into the garlic kale and was AMAZING on it! I will definitely make it that way in the future!
This is one of my family's all time favorites. We bake ours instead (toss with olive oil & garlic, spread on cookie sheet. As soon as it comes out, sprinkle with parm cheese - YUM!!!

Yum! I’m not a fan of kale, and I loved this! I did add some bacon that I had precooked, and a sprinkle of Ghost Pepper Salt. Also used one of the great tips from another reviewer and steamed the kale before sauté, and it indeed removed the bitterness! This is a keeper!

This was my first time cooking with kale, so I was really just looking for some basic cooking instructions in this recipe. The preparation in this recipe is perfect. I am really just learning to cook, so a "bunch" of kale doesn't mean a lot to me. I used about 1.5-2 cups and it was not enough. The kale really cooks down, so I would probably double that amount the next time I make this. I didn't have quite the same ingredients, so I ended up doing this a little differently. I heated up 2 TBSP of olive oil and tore the leaves from the large stalks as described, and cooked the kale for about five minutes. Once the kale began to get slightly tender I added a crushed, dried, chili pepper, and about 1 TBSP of minced garlic (jarred, pre-minced), and let that cook for five more minutes. The texture was perfect and the flavor was amazing, with none of the typical kale bitterness present.
Cut off the stems. Massage with a little olive oil first. Then steam the kale for 8 minutes.. Let cool, follow the recipe and add a shake of sea salt, Parmesan cheese and lemon juice at the table.

Used 1/2 bag prewashed cut up kale. Sauteed it with a little oil and water for 10 min. before adding minced garlic. Then cooked for about 10 more minutes. Added 1-2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, then a dash of lemon juice. Yum, yum!

Nothing new here...but a nice way to cook greens in general. Doesn't need too much oil, maybe a little less than called for, butter works well too. I recently learned about massaging Kale first...AND IT'S TRUE. It WAS less bitter, it DID reduce in volume...my new favorite thing to do to Kale to overcome the bitterness. I'll eat more as a result. Could add Red Pepper Flakes if you like heat (cook it in the oil before adding the greens). A little Kosher salt and ground black pepper during the cooking process adds flavor. I pulled the garlic out of the oil and added more later as suggested.

I sauteed mushrooms in butter first, then added a bit of olive oil and the kale and cooked for probably more like 7-10 minutes. I added a splash of chicken broth after about 5 minutes to steam in a bit more flavor. I sprinkled garlic & pepper seasoning.

Kale can be gross. This makes it great! Using fresh from the farmer's market helps, too. Sliced some "baby 'bella" mushrooms and added after the garlic and let them start giving off their liquid before adding the kale. Will make again.

This is a great way to use kale that I had left from a bunh I purchased to make soup with. It had great flavor! It's a good, quick, and easy side. Thank You for the recipe! I will definitely make this again.

It was good

Came out tasty and crispy
Pretty good
Delicious!
I add about a cup of chicken or beef broth to the kale as it cooks so that the leaves soften. Cook about 15 additional minutes covered.
Simple and delicious. For seasoning I did salt, chili powder, pepper and onion powder. Yum!
Simple, healthy and delicious

My family loved it. My son is finicky and I'm trying to get him to eat more vegetables, so it was a win. I used avocado oil instead of olive oil and added about 1/2 -3/4 cup of chicken stock. Will be making it again.
Used less oil and more garlic. It was very good. I did add some garlic herb spice grind from the store to kick up the flavor.
